analysis:
Reviewed the supplied changes: docs/developer/build.md (a head_text excerpt at lines 490-680, plus file_changes patch excerpts) and docs/developer/test.md (patch near lines 139-153 and base text). All changes are documentation only. There are no source, key-handling, attestation, encryption, authorization, or cache-storage code changes, and none of the documented behavior alters a threat-model control.

build.md patch excerpts describe: (1) scripts/install-release-cmake.sh reusing a runner-cached CMake 3.31.12 when a universal.complete marker exists and the binary reports the exact version, otherwise downloading the checksum-verified archive; (2) push runs requesting Darkbloom runner routing like same-repo PRs, with the plane approving or rejecting branches via branch_not_admitted, and fallback to literal Blacksmith labels on any error; (3) a new CI Caching section (truncated in the excerpt). test.md narrows CI cache saving to pushes on dev or master only (PRs restore and save nothing) and gates the 1.87 GB MiMo audio codec/gate on path inputs or master pushes.

Security-relevant notes for integration: the cache-save restriction to dev/master reduces cache-poisoning exposure from PR branches. The statement that the CMake archive is checksum verified and the runner-cache path is trusted rests on scripts/install-release-cmake.sh and the workflow files, which were not supplied, so the cache-reuse trust assumption (version check rather than hash check of the pre-unpacked binary) is unverified. The routing-plane admission behavior for pushed branches is also unverified. Both are CI supply-chain matters outside the provider runtime threat model (TB-002/3/7/9/11/12/13, T-041), and documentation does not establish a regression. The unchanged mention of the prefix cache (T-041) is only test-volume guidance and does not change the production gate, TTL or disk policy.

The truncated build.md patch (CI Caching section) could not be fully seen. No finding is supported by the visible evidence.
